title: Recipe 49 — Pro-grade Coder (à la Claude Code), as a spec you own

beats.label: Open the recipe
beats.cue: “A tier-1 coding agent — sub-agents, permission tiers, compaction — and none of it is hidden in a runtime.”

beats.label: Blank the scratch file
beats.cue: live/ is scratch — the committed showcase is never touched by a take.

beats.label: Load the API key
beats.cue: [needs-key] Sources demos/.env — Step 1 says run it before you read it.

groups.title: Beat 1 · Step 1 — run it first, read it after

beats.label: Open the committed spec
beats.cue: “Nearly six hundred lines. You don't type this on camera — you read it, and the recipe walks you through it section by section.”

beats.label: Lint it in place
beats.cue: “Clean, at that size, with sub-agents and permission tiers. That's what a schema buys you.”

beats.label: Compile it and check it
beats.cue: “--check: GREEN, gated at the model credential. Six hundred lines of spec, one emitted program.”

verify.note: GREEN — assertion ok; install ok; boot gated at the provider credentials gate

groups.title: Beat 2 · Steps 2–3 — the sections that make it tier-1

beats.label: Type the sub-agents block
beats.cue: “Step 2: each sub-agent gets its own tool catalog, filtered from the parent's. Delegation with a smaller blast radius.”

beats.label: Read it
beats.cue: “Note the tools list — the Task tool has to be in `tools`, not just permissions, or the child catalog comes back empty.”

beats.label: Type the permission tiers
beats.cue: “Step 3: allow, ask, deny. Deny always wins, and an allow rule can never widen a deny.”

beats.label: Read it
beats.cue: “This is the tier the security fabric recipe points back at as the runnable example.”

beats.label: Type the compaction block
beats.cue: “Step 5: compaction is not optional at this size — a long coding session will blow the window without it.”

beats.label: Find them in the emitted bundle
beats.cue: “Every one of those sections turned into ordinary code you can read.”

verify.note: the three sections, as generated code

beats.label: Read what got wired
beats.cue: “No framework indirection between the YAML and the behaviour.”

beats.label: Launch it
beats.cue: [needs-key] “Point it at this repo and ask the recipe's own opening question.”

verify.note: interactive REPL; needs a live model credential

beats.label: Ask it to explore
beats.cue: [needs-key] “Watch it delegate the wide reads to a sub-agent instead of filling its own context.”
beats.text: explore this repo and tell me what it does in three sentences

groups.title: One more thing · Step 6 — swap the model

beats.label: Read the provider table
beats.cue: “One line changes the provider. The rest of the six hundred is provider-agnostic.”

beats.label: Find the fallback chain
beats.cue: “model_fallbacks is the long-unattended-run insurance: if the primary breaker opens, turns retry down the chain instead of dying mid-goal.”

beats.label: Read it
beats.cue: “Primary and fallback, both current-generation. That's the whole failover story.”
